title: Put a number in a box
briefing: The daily report wants one figure: how many log files are in ~/logs right
now. Count them and write just that number into ~/count.txt.
The trick is feeding one command's output into another. `$(...)` runs a
command and drops its output right where you wrote it.
tips: Count lines with `wc -l`. List the logs with `ls ~/logs/*.log`.
`echo $(ls ~/logs/*.log | wc -l) > ~/count.txt` runs the count and writes the result.
objective: Count the .log files in ~/logs and write just that number into ~/count.txt.
hints: Capture a command's output with $(...): `echo $(ls ~/logs/*.log | wc -l) > ~/count.txt`.
Or pipe straight to the file: `ls ~/logs/*.log | wc -l > ~/count.txt`. There are three logs.
explanation: `$(command)` is command substitution: it runs the command and replaces itself with the output, so you can pass one command's result to another (`echo`, a variable, a condition). It's the glue that turns single commands into real scripts.
